subject: MAP: commit & monthly ramp schedule — aligning pricing and milestones
messages:
From: Nicole Barnes <nicole@atlasanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial evaluation — aligning on MAP milestones and ramp

Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Aaron and I ran a quick internal sync and we're excited about Redwood's latency profile, but we need to lock a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so our evaluation converts to production. Key asks from our procurement and platform teams:

- We need a clear monthly commit / ramp schedule (tokens per month) tied to milestone checkpoints so we can approve budget phases.
- Pricing tiers based on commit velocity — we want to understand breakpoints for discounts at 3mo / 6mo / 12mo.
- A short evaluation plan (test corpus, success criteria, smoke tests) to validate accuracy regressions during quant/latency tuning.

Do you have a template MAP you typically use? We'd like a one-page timeline that ties deliverables to payment/commit milestones. Can you draft something we can iterate on? Aaron will handle SRE acceptance criteria.

Regards,
Nicole Barnes
Head of Product, Atlas Analytics

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Nicole Barnes <nicole@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial evaluation — aligning on MAP milestones and ramp

Nicole — appreciate the clarity. I've attached an initial MAP and a draft SOW that map milestones to monthly token commitments and proposed discount tiers. High level summary below: 

- Evaluation window: 30 days (proof-of-concept) with a 3-month pilot after POC sign-off.
- Commit structure: Month 1 (pilot) 10M tokens; Month 2 25M; Month 3 50M; Month 4+ steady-state 100M/mo.
- Pricing: base rate $0.0008/token at <25M TPM, $0.0007/token 25–99M TPM, $0.0006/token >=100M TPM.
- Ramp discount: 8% after month-2 if commit achieves >=75% of planned TPM for both month 2 and 3; 12% after month-6 for sustained >=100M TPM.
- Evaluation plan: we propose three acceptance checks — latency SLA (p95 <= 280ms for short prompts), quality gate (A/B with baseline on 10k prompt set), and stability (no greater than 1% error rate for inference failures).

Next steps: Can you confirm Aaron's SRE checklist items so Dev and I can validate the smoke tests? If procurement is comfortable, we can turn this into a canary commitment and lock pricing for 90 days while you complete the evaluation.

Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (tabbed: timeline, TPM targets, pricing model), SOW-draft.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Nicole Barnes <nicole@atlasanalytics.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 08:47:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial evaluation — aligning on MAP milestones and ramp

Nicole / Aaron — looping in some technical detail on the smoke tests we recommend (short checklist):

1) Throughput staging: run 1k concurrent sessions with warm KV cache for a mix of streaming and non-streaming flows; verify p95 latency and tail behavior.
2) KV coverage: ensure prefix cache hit ratio >= 60% for the pilot dataset to evaluate cost savings.
3) Token accounting: we will provide a daily TPM report and an endpoint for checkpointed usage snapshots; confirm format you need for procurement.

For the ramp schedule, we can support the Month 1–4 numbers Marissa suggested. One ask: if Atlas needs an accelerated ramp to 150M TPM by month 5, we should agree on a step-up commit clause and a temporary overage cap to avoid surprise billing during the burst.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix to include in the MAP_v1.xlsx — Marissa, can you confirm whether we want that appended before sharing with procurement?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Nicole Barnes <nicole@atlasanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + pricing tiers — internal approval and discount ask

Marissa — quick internal note and external proposal: procurement is asking if we can make the ramp discount windows more aggressive in exchange for a larger committed term. Proposed counter-offer to Atlas: 

- 10% discount after month-2 if Atlas commits to a 12-month term (minimum 900M tokens total).
- 15% discount after month-6 for sustained >=100M TPM and an upfront 3-month partial prepay (applied to month 1–3).

Rationale: we need a booked ARR commitment to justify the preferential pricing to our finance team. If Atlas wants flexibility but lower up-front commitment, maintain the original tiered discounts (8% / 12%) with a shorter 6- or 9-month term.

Priya will help finalize the contract language and the commit enforcement wording (soft vs. hard consumption commitments). Priya, please prepare a short clause for the SOW that clarifies measurement windows and remediation for under-delivery (crediting vs. true-up).

Marissa — feel free to push this to Nicole as an option.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Nicole Barnes <nicole@atlasanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@finlytics.io>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + pricing tiers — internal approval and discount ask

Marissa / Team — thanks, this is helpful. Atlas leadership reviewed the options and we're willing to agree to a 12-month committed term if you can accept the 10% discount after month-2 (we can meet the 900M minimal total commitment). We also want the technical appendix Dev mentioned in the MAP and a daily TPM usage feed.

Action items we expect in the next 48 hours:
- Redwood: return a redlined SOW with the 12-month commit and 10% kick-in clause, include technical appendix and daily usage endpoint details (Priya to lead contract language).
- Atlas: internal signature path for PO; Aaron will confirm SRE smoke-test checklist by Monday.

If we can get the SOW redline and a DocuSign link, we can target an April 20th effective date and an April 24th pilot start.

Nicole Barnes
Head of Product, Atlas Analytics

Attachments referenced: SOW-draft.pdf
